description: Evals for the check-bash-read PreToolUse hook

evals.name: cat-large-file
evals.reason: Plain cat on large file — should deny

evals.name: cat-small-file
evals.reason: Small file — not worth delegating

evals.name: cat-with-flag
evals.reason: cat with -n flag — should still deny

evals.name: head-default-count
evals.reason: Bare head reads 10 lines — bounded, like a targeted Read

evals.name: head-with-count
evals.reason: head -100 is bounded under the threshold — same policy as offset/limit

evals.name: tail-default-count
evals.reason: Bare tail reads 10 lines — bounded

evals.name: less-large-file
evals.reason: less dumps the whole file non-interactively — deny

evals.name: cat-pipe
evals.reason: Piped command — targeted read

evals.name: cat-redirect
evals.reason: Redirect — copying file, not reading into context

evals.name: non-read-command
evals.reason: Not a file read command

evals.name: grep-command
evals.reason: grep is a targeted search — not caught

evals.name: cat-quoted-path
evals.reason: Quoted path — should still be caught

evals.name: cat-nonexistent
evals.reason: File doesn't exist — let Bash handle the error

evals.name: empty-command
evals.reason: Empty command — pass through

evals.name: missing-command-field
evals.reason: No command field — pass through

evals.name: more-large-file
evals.reason: more dumps the whole file non-interactively — deny

evals.name: head-n-space-count
evals.reason: -n and its count parsed as one flag — 5 lines is bounded

evals.name: head-count-over-threshold
evals.reason: A count above the threshold is a bulk read wearing head's clothes

evals.name: chained-command
evals.reason: A read anywhere in a chain still lands in context

evals.name: semicolon-chain
evals.reason: Semicolon chains are judged per segment

evals.name: leading-whitespace
evals.reason: A leading space used to defeat the anchored match

evals.name: path-with-spaces
evals.reason: Quoted path containing a space survives argument splitting

evals.name: minified-single-line
evals.reason: One 200KB line — the byte ceiling catches what a line count cannot

evals.name: unreadable-file
evals.reason: Unreadable file falls through to Bash, which reports the real error

evals.name: double-dash-path
evals.reason: -- ends flag parsing; the path after it is still a path
